title: Kubernetes Service Discovery
description: Learn how Kubernetes provides built-in service discovery for containerized microservices.

data.text: Kubernetes has revolutionized microservices deployment by providing built-in service discovery, load balancing, and self-healing. Google, which created Kubernetes ( Borg), runs billions of containers weekly and relies on Kubernetes for service discovery at massive scale.

Kubernetes uses CoreDNS to provide DNS-based service discovery. Each Service gets a stable DNS name like my-service.namespace.svc.cluster.local. Pods can discover each other using these names without any external registry.

data.title: Kubernetes Service Types
items: ClusterIP: Exposes service on an internal cluster IP (default)
NodePort: Exposes service on each node's IP at a static port
LoadBalancer: Provisions a cloud load balancer (AWS ELB, GCP LB)
ExternalName: Maps service to external DNS name

data.title: Headless Services
data.text: Headless Services (clusterIP: None) disable load balancing and return all pod IPs. This is useful for stateful applications like databases or when you need client-side load balancing.

data.title: Example: Kubernetes Service Definition
data.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: user-service
  namespace: production
spec:
  selector:
    app: user-service
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  type: ClusterIP
---
# DNS name: user-service.production.svc.cluster.local

items.question: Do I still need Consul in Kubernetes?
items.answer: Not always. Kubernetes DNS and Services cover many use cases. Use Consul if you need cross-cluster service discovery or advanced traffic management.

items.question: What is kube-proxy?
items.answer: kube-proxy runs on every node and maintains network rules to route traffic to Services. It uses iptables or IPVS for load balancing.

items.question: How does Kubernetes handle service health?
items.answer: Kubernetes uses liveness and readiness probes. Unhealthy pods are removed from Service endpoints automatically.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Kubernetes provides built-in DNS-based service discovery
Services provide stable IPs and DNS names
Health probes keep Service endpoints healthy
data.takeaway: Kubernetes eliminates the need for external service registries in many cases.
